title: Fix cross-model leakage in per-model share charts after quota reshuffle
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Symptom: Console per-model 'Percent of Total' and per-model leaderboard charts show transient spikes where unrelated models capture ~10-40% of traffic for 30-90 minute windows following quota reshuffle maintenance. This inflates costs and misleads customers about their top models.

Scope: Affects percent-of-total and per-model breakdown panes in the Console for customers who experienced a quota pool reallocation event between 2025-02-12 and 2025-02-14. Not all customers; higher risk for Dedicated tenants with sharded metering agents.

Hypothesis: During the quota reshuffle job we temporarily updated model->quota_bucket assignments before rollup metadata propagated to the aggregation workers. The metering pipeline applies the bucket tag to in-flight aggregate windows using a short-lived in-memory mapping. If a model's bucket mapping changes mid-window, late-arriving partial aggregates were stamped with the new bucket but merged into older windows that were already attributed to the previous bucket, causing double-counting or apparent transfers of percent share across models.

Reproduction steps:
1) Run a staging quota-reshuffle tool to swap bucket assignments for a subset of models.
2) Inject streaming usage events with interleaved timestamps that span the reshuffle boundary.
3) Observe per-window attribution in the rollup service (rollup-v2) and Console's timeseries join that computes percent-of-total.

Impact analysis:
- Visibility: Console charts show misleading top model lists for affected intervals.
- Billing: Tenant-level totals remain correct due to eventual reconciliation, but per-model breakdowns used for advisory quota alerts and customer-facing insights are wrong until reconciliation completes.

Mitigation and proposal:
1) Short-term: Disable live quota-reshuffle ops during peak windows and add a conservative quiesce period (5 minutes) where rollup workers ignore mapping changes for in-flight windows. Implement a feature flag to toggle quiesce.
2) Long-term: Make model->bucket assignment part of the immutable event envelope on ingest. Ensure assignment version is included in streaming events so late-arriving fragments are merged by assignment version instead of current mapping.
3) Backfill plan: Run an idempotent attribution rescan for affected windows using event-versioned assignments to correct percent-of-total charts. Add an audit metric for the size of corrections.

Acceptance criteria:
- New quiesce flag prevents misattribution during reshuffles in staging and is validated against synthetic tests.
- Backfill job exists and corrects a sample tenant's charts to within 1% of expected distribution.
- Console shows a visible note on corrected intervals and an audit log entry with correction delta.

Metrics and queries:
- Dashboard: rollup/attribution-mismatch-count, rollup/reshuffle-events, console/corrections-applied
- Ad-hoc query: SELECT window_start, model_id, sum(tokens) FROM rollup_v2 WHERE assignment_version != window_assignment_version GROUP BY ...

Rollout steps:
- PRs: rollup service change, ingestion envelope change, Console annotation UI
- Canary: 5 tenants in us-west for 48 hours
- Full rollout: after 72h monitoring

Related artifacts:
- Repro harness: github.com/redwood-inference/metering/repro/reshuffle-harness (branch: fix-attr-2025)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/usage/percent-share
- Incident notes: Confluence /spaces/OPS/pages/QA-reshuffle-2025-02
